newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Strategic privatisation bid fails.
newsitem.headline: China Strategic privatisation bid fails.

text.p: The bid by the chairman of China Strategic Holdings Ltd to privatise the company has failed, the company said in a notice published on Thursday.

China Strategic and Sanion Enterprises Ltd, a company owned and controlled by China Strategic chairman Oei Hong Leong, said the offer for shares and warrants in China Strategic had closed with Oei and Sanion acquiring less than 50 percent of the company.
The parties acquired only a total of 41.59 percent of the issued shares and 48.13 percent of the outstanding warrants.
Immediately prior to the offer on November 4, the parties held 36.25 percent of the enlarged issued share capital of the company and 48.12 percent of the warrants.
Oei raised his offer on November 11 to $2.80 from $2.50 for each ordinary share, while his offer of HK$0.29 for each warrant was unchanged.
All shareholders and warrantholders who tendered their shares and warrants will have them returned to them within 10 days, the notice said.
In early trade on Thursday, China Strategic shares were untraded at HK$2.80 and its warrant was untraded at HK$0.31.
